title: Skin without Underwear
content:
I want to create underwear and need to use an avatar without underwear texture to use it for my presentation. I'm not able to change the skin in the newest CLO version. How can I solve this problem? In addition the question: is it possible that the avatars like Feifei can be added back to the default garment avatars? I was always using FeiFei and like to continue using her.

Hope we can find a solution.

Sophie

PS.: In my opinion the new way of reaching the library is not an improvement.

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Hi There. For the newer Avatars the undergarments can be set to nude, this has been a feature in CLO for several versions now. You can click on the avatar and the go to the Property Editor > Body Styling > Click on the blue head icon to the right on Skin Style > a pop up will open > Change underwear from Covered to NudeAs for older Avatars these will not be added back to to CLO library. But if you wish to continue using FeiFei you can open an old CLO project where you used FeiFei and then go to File > Save As Avatar. You can save FeiFei, just make sure to save to your local computer/sharedirve and not to the CLO program folders as those can be replaced when CLO is updated in the future.Also, keep in mind that FeiFei and older avatars will not have some of the newer features like bust adjustment, soft body, or the above mentioned Skin Style options
content_description: This web page aims to provide solutions for using and customizing underwear-free avatars in CLO, address the possibility of reintegrating popular avatars like FeiFei into the default library, and gather user feedback on recent interface changes.

title: Unlocking VMOD Magic Outside CLO: Fur Strand Breakthrough!
content:
* * *

Hi everyone!  
I’m **beyond excited** to share something I just discovered that completely **changed my workflow** – and I _had_ to post it here because I know I can’t be the only one who needed this!

🔍 I’ve always loved working with **VMODs** for fabrics in CLO, but as someone who renders mainly in external software (Unreal, Blender, etc.), I always felt limited – like I was missing the full power of those textures outside of CLO. Until now.

✨ I started experimenting with **Fur Strands inside VMODs** , and the results blew my mind. Turns out, you can totally **bake strand-based effects directly into the 3D model** , and then render them outside of CLO – without rebuilding the entire shader from scratch. No more starting from zero to simulate that delicate fiber look!

* * *

🔄 Before & After – Render Comparison

![1909bd239af846589b549ce418e393bd](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202505/2014fe3da04741ff949f9c1465d403b7/images/1909bd239af846589b549ce418e393bd1.png)**Left:** VMOD 3D with Fur Strand  
**Right:** Original VMOD 3D  
What’s crazy is this used to be **just a render-time effect**. But now… it’s **actual geometry inside the 3D view**! No tricks, no illusions – those fibers are **real mesh strands** you can see and work with before even hitting render.

* * *

### 🧵 True 3D Vision – No More “Render-Only” Magic

![41a5e9f5e5e7453185cdf320e069adf4](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202505/2014fe3da04741ff949f9c1465d403b7/images/41a5e9f5e5e7453185cdf320e069adf42.png)

On the left: **VMOD with Fur Strand** – you can clearly see the strand geometry right inside the 3D viewport.  
On the right: Original VMOD – the texture is there, but it’s just a visual placeholder until render.  
  
And here’s the amazing part:

🔁 **Once you copy over the fur settings** (shape, density, roughness map, etc.),  
🎯 The **final render looks almost identical** to the original!  
But now you’re working with actual geometry — not a preset shader effect that only comes alive at render time.

This opens up a whole new world of flexibility:  
✅ You can preview and tweak fur in real time.  
✅ Export it to external engines like Unreal or Blender.  
✅ And finally bridge the gap between **hyperrealism and workflow control**.  


* * *

### 💡 Why This Matters (at least to me!)

This discovery means:

  * I can **re-use** my entire library of custom VMODs outside CLO.

  * No need to rebuild complex shaders in other tools.

  * Textures look **richer, fuzzier, and closer to real fabric** , especially for knits, fleece, and delicate materials.




Honestly, it felt like unlocking a **secret power-up**. If you’ve ever wanted to push the realism of your renders while keeping a smooth pipeline, **this is for you**.

* * *

### 🔧 Super Tip!

When transitioning from _Fur Render_ (render-only) to _Fur Strand_ (real-time), some settings reset or behave differently — but with a few adjustments, you can recreate the original look or even enhance it.

Here’s my personal checklist and advanced tips after testing:

✅ **Base, Normal, Metallic, Displacement texture**  
→ This is preserved. No changes needed.

⚠️ **Fur parameters**  
→ These reset, so you’ll need to reapply:

  * Hair shape

  * Shine

  * Gravity

  * Curl

  * Variation

  * **Roughness** → Switch from value to **map** input for more accurate surface behavior.

  * **Density & Seed** → Play with different seed settings to discover subtle or dramatic variations. A single seed change can alter the entire flow without touching the base design.




🌓 **Opacity Map**  
→ I recommend **increasing contrast** , especially in darker areas, to restore the sense of translucency and depth seen in the original render. Without this, the material can look flat or less realistic.

🧩 **Custom Density Mapping (Advanced)**  
→ If your fabric has different fur behavior in specific areas (e.g. front vs. sides), unlink them:

  * Separate the textile into **front and side sections** using the properties editor

  * This lets you control **density, length, and hair direction** by faces.




* * *

### 🗣️ I’d love to hear from others:

Have you tried integrating strand-based textures into your external workflow?  
Any tips, feedback, or renders you want to share?

  
👀 Can you tell which one this is?  
  
![fbd6d41e40ae4f5c973bdb717e841ef8](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202505/2014fe3da04741ff949f9c1465d403b7/images/fbd6d41e40ae4f5c973bdb717e841ef8VMOD%203D%20ORIGINAL.png)

Thanks for reading!  
— Seer  
![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202505/2014fe3da04741ff949f9c1465d403b7/images/a356275c837f4137ac1e77ca099f22c63.png)

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: GOOD ONE !👍🏻

Comment 2: Amazing ❤️!!!

Comment 3: Hi Sofia, this was a great read - thank you for sharing! Regarding the transition process from Fur Rendr Only to Fur Strand, we plan to enhance it by automatically preserving the parameters across two Fur fabric types. 🙂
Reply 1: If they do that, it would be even more amazing. Each new version is a chance to improve the current workflow. 😍

Comment 4: Thank you for taking the time to share such a detailed comparison and review😍 Your feedback has been incredibly valuable to us. We truly appreciate hearing from you—whether it's positive or constructive, your insights help us grow and improve. Please continue to share your thoughts with us!❤️

title: Patricia’s Digital Prairie: Stitching the West in CLO
content:
## _Patricia Nahorniac (_[__@deadstockbloom__](https://www.instagram.com/deadstockbloom/) _) is redefining digital fashion with a blend of craftsmanship and innovation. From her roots in textile design to pushing creative boundaries with CLO, she brings garments to life beyond physical limits. In this interview, she shares the inspirations, tools, and techniques behind her latest project._

* * *

![25c5345dc8cf4bc2959f2acc22f9971a](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202505/3bbd1710e68f495c9b71321801eb7083/images/25c5345dc8cf4bc2959f2acc22f9971adeadstockbloom-CLO-Banner.png)

### **Can you introduce yourself and share a bit about your background?**

Hello, I’m Patricia Nahorniac or @deadstockbloom. I’m a Digital Fashion Specialist and CLO Creator from Romania and I’m currently based in Berlin, Germany.

My design journey started when I began studying Textile Design at Design Academy Eindhoven (NL). After my studies, I had my own sustainable clothing business. Through this experience I learned a lot about clothes making.

I started working in CLO because I wanted to try something new. The software is quite intuitive to learn if you’re already familiar with sewing. So far, I’ve collaborated with creators, artists and fashion brands to digitize clothing concepts for use in advertising campaigns or product visualizations.

**Could you share the story or inspiration behind this project?**

This artwork is part of a series that explores the various visual qualities of “Leather”. The inspiration for the suede look came from vintage Western Clothing, Cowboys and all the beautiful details and patchworks applied to these garments. I thought it would be a nice opportunity to explore working with graphics, floral motifs and gradients. 

  
![5d5b1200b15d4b0ca04fe3c26fff5959](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202505/3bbd1710e68f495c9b71321801eb7083/images/5d5b1200b15d4b0ca04fe3c26fff5959deadstockbloom_Suede-Leather-Look_moodboard.png)

**How do you usually approach planning and preparing for a new project? We'd also love to hear about your typical routine.**

Generally, I’ll start with choosing a theme and collecting references. I like finding images in old books, looking through online archives and museum websites such as “The Met”. 

Afterwards, I either sketch a garment/outfit or start directly with creating patterns in CLO. I’ll usually make modifications as I go, depending on the style/fit I’m looking for. The next step would be posing the Avatar and preparing for texturing. Once this step is completed, all that’s left is creating a scene in Blender (adding a background and nice lighting) and rendering out the final result. 

  
**What was your favorite part of creating these artworks using CLO?**

For this artwork, my favorite part of the process was to create floral patchworks that could have detailed topstitching. I’m quite happy with how this effect turned out, but it took a bit of time and patience to put everything together. This is also one of the things I love about CLO - it can be a super fast and powerful tool, but you can also spend hours on intricate details and feel almost like a digital artisan.

  
![5fa71c3713f94501ae5fa4015554cb3a](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202505/3bbd1710e68f495c9b71321801eb7083/images/5fa71c3713f94501ae5fa4015554cb3adeadstockbloom-Suede-Leather-Look_03.png)![6c36cc1c04bb470daf74a10ce740fb61](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202505/3bbd1710e68f495c9b71321801eb7083/images/6c36cc1c04bb470daf74a10ce740fb61deadstockbloom-Suede-Leather-Look_02.jpg)

**Which feature in CLO did you find most useful while working on this project?**

I think I used the Trace Graphic feature the most. It’s really amazing to be able to create intricate patterns in just a few seconds. This feature really saves up hours in pattern tracing and definitely makes the process much smoother. I also really like adding details through thickness, topstitching and trims. It was quite fun to use buttons in a more playful way. 

**Are there any artists, designers, or movements that have influenced your creative approach?**

I’m inspired by workwear and utility clothing. I love overalls and garments that have a lot of pockets. Another nice reference for me is Fruits Magazine, I can always find inspiration for outfits by looking at street style looks from Japan.  


**What tips would you share with aspiring digital fashion designers who wish to follow a path like yours?**

As a tip, I would say it’s good to find a balance between creativity and being technical. You should try out different styles until you’re able to create your own. Lastly, always post your work! I think that social media is a great way to get to know other creators and find opportunities.

  
  
![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202505/3bbd1710e68f495c9b71321801eb7083/images/f99f908a0b2a46cd81a8b4fd8db74d36deadstockbloom-Suede-Leather-Look_01.jpg)

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Sooo amazing!

Comment 2: Perfect 😍

Comment 3: Just one motion : 😍❤️Excellent work!

Comment 4: amazing work 👏
content_description: Discover how Patricia Nahorniac (@deadstockbloom) merges craftsmanship and digital innovation to create stunning virtual fashion designs using CLO.
